pathwayLabel: No Reciprocity — Standard Texas Journeyman Route
steps: TDLR's out-of-state page lists Texas's reciprocity states. Florida is on neither list: Journeyman (Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Nebraska, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Dakota and Wyoming) or Master (Alabama, Arkansas, Iowa, Louisiana, Nebraska, North Carolina and Ohio). TDLR adds: "Currently there are no reciprocal licensing agreements for any other license types."

Without reciprocity, you apply through Texas's standard Journeyman Electrician route. TDLR requires at least 7,000 hours of on-the-job training under the supervision of a Master Electrician licensed in Texas to take the exam, and 8,000 hours for licensure, documented on TDLR's Experience Verification Form.
Whether TDLR credits experience gained in Florida toward those hours is not stated on TDLR's Journeyman page. Ask TDLR before you plan around it.
Pay TDLR's non-refundable $30 Journeyman application fee.
Pass the Journeyman Electrician exam administered by PSI. The exam fee is $78, per PSI's TDLR Electrician Candidate Information Bulletin, which TDLR's exam page links to.
Await processing. TDLR does not publish a processing timeline on its out-of-state licensing page.
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-01 from TDLR's own pages, replacing earlier generator template steps ($235 fee, 32 training hours) that contradicted the $108 total. Sources: reciprocity lists and license fees from TDLR's out-of-state page (https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/electricians/out-of-state.htm). Hours requirement and $30 application fee from TDLR's Journeyman Electrician page (https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/electricians/apply/individuals/journeyman-electrician.htm). $78 exam fee from PSI's TDLR Electrician Candidate Information Bulletin (https://test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/1682), linked from TDLR's exam page. $108 = $30 + $78. This page covers the Journeyman license only; Master requirements for non-reciprocal applicants were not researched for this record. No figure for crediting out-of-state experience is published, so none is assumed.
officialSourceName: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)
